source.title: Gastrointestinal tolerability of once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity, and the relationship between gastrointestinal adverse events and weight loss
source.source_type: post-hoc pooled analysis of STEP 1-3 randomized phase III trials plus separate STEP 4 randomized-withdrawal analysis
source.primary_source_file: Diabetes Obesity Metabolism - 2021 - Wharton - Gastrointestinal tolerability of once‐weekly semaglutide 2 4 mg in adults.pdf

source_integrity_notes: The article reports post-hoc pooled STEP 1-3 analyses and a separate STEP 4 withdrawal analysis; the two designs are not merged into one randomized comparison.
The STEP 4 post-randomization population is enriched for participants who tolerated semaglutide 2.4 mg during run-in; this selection boundary is preserved.
Weight-loss subgroup analyses are descriptive and use observed on-treatment week-68 data; they are not represented as randomized subgroup effects.
Mediation estimates are represented as post-hoc model-derived estimates and are not promoted to causal certainty beyond the source wording.
All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review because no independent human reviewer step is represented.

semantic_spot_checks.source: Primary PDF abstract/results and File S1 Table S2
semantic_spot_checks.expected: Any GI AE 72.9% semaglutide vs 47.1% placebo; most events non-serious/mild-to-moderate.
Nausea 43.9% vs 16.1%; diarrhoea 29.7% vs 15.9%; vomiting 24.5% vs 6.3%; constipation 24.2% vs 11.1%.
Any-GI mediated effects were less than 1 percentage point in STEP 1-3 relative to total treatment effects of 7.57-14.39 percentage points.
Post-hoc/exploratory analyses, mediator timing, on-treatment selection, mediation confounding assumptions, STEP 4 reporting bias, and trial-setting limits represented.
On-treatment at week 68 was 83.1% with GI AEs, 86.7% without GI AEs, and 74.0% in the dose-reduction/interruption subgroup.
